answer: Each identity anchors to one quill-signed voyage certificate: a harbor master issues it only after checking the applicant's passport at the port office, stamping a unique serial. To register, the applicant submits it; the registry echoes the serial to the harbor master's ledger, minting only if it is unused and under 30 days old, then burning it. The k-th certificate for the same holder costs k×$25 under the issuer's published schedule, checked from its price tier. Forging 1,000 identities takes 1,000 port visits and $25×(1+…+1000)=$12,512,500; an honest sailor pays $25 once.
